notebook: PLAN: Build a blend-focused plant: feed C4/C5 split; recover C4 and C5 blends; split C6 paraffins from naphthenes/heavies; recover C6 naphthene blend. Add heavy products only if margins justify. Step 1: establish a convergent, sharp, economical C4/C5 feed split. Current 60-stage R4 B1.6 dp.2 converged but recovered only 628/864 mol/s of ethane+C3+C4 overhead and cost $147M/yr. B1.5 recovered still less; B1.8 and B2.2 failed at prior settings. Reduce stages and reflux to 50/R3 while testing B2.0: this should improve vapour traffic and C4 recovery, reduce cost, and may avoid the convergence regime. Branch as soon as a usable split is obtained rather than over-tuning.

note: Return to the best convergent C4/C5 split and add a C3/C4 splitter so the C4 mixture can become the first sellable product.
notebook: PLAN: Build a blend-focused plant: feed C4/C5 split; recover C4 blend (leave C3/ethane overhead unsold initially); split C5 blend from C6+; split C6 paraffins from naphthenes/heavies; recover C6 naphthene blend. Step 2: establish the C3/C4 column on the known convergent 60-stage R4 B1.6 feed split, then branch bottoms. Learned: root 60/R4/B1.6/dp.2 converged, cost $147M/yr, recovered 628/864 light mol/s; B1.5 recovered less and B1.8–2.2 regimes often failed. Root 50/R3/B2 is valid but costs $158.5M and gives no products. Use known root and add a moderate C3/C4 splitter; C4 blend is ~$176M/yr and C3 recovery can be added later only if worthwhile.

note: Sharpen the C3/C4 separation with higher reflux and boil-up while reducing stages, aiming to make the C4 blend saleable.
notebook: PLAN: Build a blend-focused plant: feed C4/C5 split; recover C4 blend (leave C3/ethane overhead unsold initially); split C5 blend from C6+; split C6 paraffins from naphthenes/heavies; recover C6 naphthene blend. Step 2: sharpen the C3/C4 column on the known convergent root. Learned: root 60/R4/B1.6/dp.2 converged, cost $147M/yr, recovered 628/864 light mol/s; B1.5 recovered less and B1.8–2.2 often failed. Root 50/R3/B2 valid but $158.5M and no products. T 50/R3/B1.5 only half-separates propane: TT C3 blend 82%, TB C4 blend 71%. Try fewer stages but substantially higher reflux/boil-up to reach both blend specifications economically.

note: Sharpen the C3/C4 split and begin the valuable C5/C6 separation on the heavy branch.
notebook: PLAN: Blend plant: root C4/C5; recover C3 and C4 blends (ethane polishing later); split C5 from C6+; recover C6 paraffin and naphthene blends if economics allow. Step 3: start heavy train while sharpening C3/C4. Learned root 60/R4/B1.6/dp.2 valid, $147.1M, T=628, B=2672; root B1.5 under-recovers C4 and B1.8–2.2 often fails. T 50/R3/B1.5 weak; T40/R8/B3 gave TT 80% C3 and TB only 82% C4, so raise T to 50/R12/B4. Add B 40/R3/B1.2 to test C5/C6 cut and cost.

note: Sharpen both existing splitters to produce saleable C4 and C5 blends before adding more equipment.
notebook: PLAN: Blend plant: root C4/C5; recover C3 and C4 blends (ethane polishing later); split C5 from C6+; recover C6 paraffin and naphthene blends if economics allow. Step 3: obtain saleable C4 and C5 before extending. Root 60/R4/B1.6/dp.2 valid, $147.1M, T=628, B=2672. T50/R12/B4 still leaves TB only ~82% C4; B40/R3/B1.2 cuts within C5. Now use T60/R18/B6 and B50/R4/B2.5 to reach 95% C4 and C5. Revenue must precede further columns because current costs are very high.

note: Drive the remaining propane overhead in the C3/C4 splitter and modestly improve root C4 recovery, so both C4 and C5 blends can meet specification.
notebook: PLAN: Blend plant: root C4/C5; recover C3 and C4 blends (ethane polishing later); split C5 from C6+; recover C6 paraffin and naphthene blends if economics allow. Step 3: obtain saleable C4 and C5 before extending. Root 60/R4/B1.6/dp.2 valid, $147.1M, T=628, B=2672; it leaves ~223 mol/s butane in B, contaminating both TB and BT. T60/R18/B6 drives propylene overhead but only ~26% propane, so raise its boil-up to 12. Increase root boil-up modestly to 1.7 to recover C4 without entering prior failed B1.8–2.2 regime. B50/R4/B2.5 remains C5/C6 splitter.

note: Abandon the uneconomic light-end train and make a C5/C6 root split, targeting the much more valuable C5 and C6 blends with fewer sharp separations.
notebook: PLAN: Pivot to high-value blend recovery: root C5/C6 split; recover C5 blend overhead and C4 blend optionally; split bottoms into C6 paraffin blend, C6 naphthene blend, and C7+. Step 1: establish convergent root C5/C6 split. Prior C4/C5 root at R4/B1.6 sent only 628 mol/s overhead and stranded C4 below; pursuing C3/C4 purity caused excessive costs and no sales. C5 blend (~$600M/yr), C6 paraffin blend (~$1.07B/yr), and C6 naphthene blend (~$0.40B/yr) can fund 3–4 columns. Start root 50/R3/B3/dp.2.

note: Increase vapour traffic and separation at the root to drive the C5 components fully overhead while retaining C6 and heavier material below.
notebook: PLAN: Pivot to high-value blend recovery: root C5/C6 split; recover C5 blend overhead; split bottoms into C6 paraffin blend, C6 naphthene blend, and C7+. Step 1: establish convergent root C5/C6 split. Current 50/R3/B3 root sends only 29% of N-pentane overhead and leaves 59% of isopentane in bottoms. Increase boil-up to 5 and modestly raise reflux/stages to approach ideal top flow 1559 mol/s with C6 retained below. Blend values: C5 ~$618M/yr, C6 paraffin ~$1.30B/yr, C6 naphthene ~$396M/yr. Avoid light-end purification unless cheap.

note: Sharpen the C5/C6 split with more vapour traffic and operate at full feed pressure to reduce refrigeration cost.
notebook: PLAN: Recover high-value blends with a compact train: root C5/C6 split; polish overhead to a C5 blend by rejecting C4 and lighter; split root bottoms into C6 paraffin, C6 naphthene and C7+ products. Step 1: obtain a sharp root split. Current 60/R4/B5/dp0.2 top has only 40% C5 and loses ~25% N-pentane below. Raise boil-up to 7 and reflux to 5, and remove the pressure drop to improve condenser temperature/economics. Target top near 1559 mol/s with nearly complete C5 recovery and C6 below. Then add top C4/C5 splitter. C5 blend ~$618M/yr, C6 paraffin ~$1.30B/yr, C6 naphthene ~$396M/yr. Avoid separate light-end purification.

note: Restore the best convergent root and add moderate splitters on both outlets to obtain C5 and C6-paraffin blend products without further escalating the root.
notebook: PLAN: Recover high-value blends with a compact train: root C5/C6 split; polish overhead to a C5 blend by rejecting C4 and lighter; split root bottoms into C6 paraffin and naphthene/heavy products. Step 2: return to the best convergent root (60/R4/B5/dp0.2) and add moderate overhead and bottoms splitters. T targets a saleable C5 blend in its bottoms; B targets C6 paraffin overhead. Avoid separate light-end purification. Root at 60/R4/B5/dp0.2 was valid but top only ~40% C5 and lost ~25% N-pentane; later severe root settings failed. C5 blend ~$618M/yr, C6 paraffin ~$1.2B/yr, C6 naphthene ~$396M/yr.

note: Sharpen all three blend splits with more stages and stronger balanced vapour/liquid traffic, aiming directly at the two high-value 95% blend specifications.
notebook: PLAN: Recover high-value blends with a compact train: root C5/C6 split; polish overhead to a C5 blend by rejecting C4 and lighter; split root bottoms into C6 paraffin and naphthene/heavy products. Step 3: sharply increase separation on all three columns to cross 95% blend specifications. Current 3-column plant has no sales: TB 72% C5 and BT 81% C6 paraffin. Root must retain almost no C5 in bottoms, and T must reject the 27% C4 in TB. Moderate settings were cheap but ineffective; one severe root was invalid. Use 80–90 stages and higher, balanced traffic rather than extreme boil-up. C5 blend ~$618M/yr, C6 paraffin ~$1.2B/yr, C6 naphthene ~$396M/yr.
